title: Washington's 9th Congressional District election, 2026
description: Washington's 9th Congressional District covers parts of King County and Pierce County, including portions of Seattle, Tacoma, and the surrounding suburbs. Incumbent Democrat Adam Smith, first elected in 1996 and the dean of Washington's House delegation, is seeking a 16th term. Smith faces a competitive top-two primary on August 4, 2026, featuring challengers from the left (Kshama Sawant, a former Seattle city councilmember running as an independent socialist; Melissa Chaudhry, a fellow Democrat; and Jacob Perasso of the Socialist Workers Party) and the right (Republican Doug Basler, a perennial candidate). The district is safely Democratic (Cook PVI D+23) and the race is rated Safe/Solid D by Cook, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball. The top-two finishers will advance to the November 3, 2026 general election.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found specifically for the 2026 race in Washington's 9th Congressional District as of mid-2026. Surveys from 2024 showed Smith with comfortable leads over his general-election opponents, but no 2026 cycle polling has been published.

candidates.name: D. Adam Smith
candidates.summary: Adam Smith has represented Washington's 9th Congressional District in the U.S. House since 1997 and is the dean of the Washington state House delegation. He chairs the House Armed Services Committee as Ranking Member and previously served as its chair from 2019 to 2023. A moderate-to-liberal Democrat, Smith is a member of both the New Democrat Coalition and the Congressional Progressive Caucus.

career_history.title: U.S. Representative
career_history.description: Representing Washington's 9th Congressional District. Served as Chair (2019-2023) and Ranking Member (2023-present) of the House Armed Services Committee.

career_history.title: State Senator
career_history.description: Represented the 33rd legislative district. Elected at age 25, the youngest state senator in the country at that time.

career_history.title: Prosecutor

candidates.name: Douglas Michael Basler
candidates.summary: Doug Basler is a Republican candidate who has run against Adam Smith in previous cycles, including the 2020 and 2022 general elections. He is a perennial conservative challenger in Washington's 9th Congressional District.

candidates.name: Melissa Chaudhry
candidates.summary: Melissa Chaudhry is a Democratic candidate running for the 9th Congressional District seat. She previously ran in the 2024 top-two primary against incumbent Adam Smith, receiving 30.4% of the vote.

candidates.name: Kshama Sawant
candidates.summary: Kshama Sawant is a socialist politician and former Seattle City Councilmember who served from 2014 to 2024. She is running for U.S. Congress as an independent with a progressive platform focused on economic justice, Medicare for All, and housing reform. Sawant is a prominent figure in the socialist movement and previously founded the Seattle chapter of Socialist Alternative.

candidates.name: Jacob Perasso
candidates.summary: Jacob Perasso is the Socialist Workers Party candidate for Washington's 9th Congressional District in 2026. The Socialist Workers Party is a Marxist political party running on an anti-capitalist platform.

forecast.rationale: No public 2026 polling exists for this race, which tempers confidence. However, structural factors are overwhelmingly favorable to Democrats: Cook PVI D+23, unanimous Safe/Solid D ratings from Cook, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball, and a long-serving incumbent (Adam Smith, first elected 1996, dean of the Washington delegation, ranking member on House Armed Services). The challenger field is fragmented among a perennial Republican (Basler), a fellow Democrat (Chaudhry, who got 30.4% in the 2024 top-two primary), an independent socialist with name recognition (Sawant), and a Socialist Workers Party candidate (Perasso). In a D+23 district, even the best-positioned challenger faces an extremely steep climb, and the splintered opposition further advantages the incumbent. The top-two primary on August 4 will be competitive for the second slot, but regardless of which opponent emerges, the general election outcome is not in doubt.
